project_tracker_diagnostic: Blue-green/glaucous obovate to elliptic leaves, pale papery/scaly bark, and small oblong/barrel-shaped acorns often flattened at both ends.
verified_target_counties: Hays; Travis; Blanco; Comal; Bandera; Edwards; Gillespie; Kerr; Real; Uvalde; Val Verde

morphology_keys.habit: Small deciduous tree, often on limestone hills, canyons, streamsides, and Edwards Plateau woodlands.
morphology_keys.leaves: Blue-green/glaucous, obovate or elliptic; margin entire to shallowly lobed; underside whitish/glaucous with stellate hairs when young.
morphology_keys.acorn: Cup shallow; nut oblong or barrel-shaped and often flattened at both ends.
best_field_traits: FNA: leaf blade typically 40–90 × 30–60 mm; elliptic to obovate, very blue-green and glaucous, usually rounded or retuse at the tip; shade leaves can be deeply lobed.
Leaf underside initially with erect stellate hairs that often shed as the leaf matures, leaving a pale glaucous surface; do not require permanent dense hairs.
Twigs initially erect-stellate pubescent, later glabrous; mature buds 1.5–3 mm long.
Mature acorn typically oblong/barrel-like, 13–15 mm long (range 11–20 mm), often flattened at both ends; cup 4–7 mm deep, moderately tuberculate and enclosing at most about 1/3 nut.
morphology_keys.joey_field_note: Joey's West Texas landscaping frame is an excellent field example of the blue-green/glaucous leaf surface and lobed foliage. Use that glaucous cast as an early cue, then confirm bark and acorn characters.

photo_strategy.oak_specific_tightening: Prioritize multi-photo late-summer/fall observations to increase the chance of mature leaves and acorns, plus curated taxon reference photos.

look_here_first: Start with several mature blue-green, glaucous leaves—not a single shade leaf. A broadly rounded or notched tip, pale papery/scaly bark, and a barrel-shaped nut whose ends can look flattened are the useful combination. If the plant is shrubby, compare the twig and cupule carefully with white shin oak.

diagnostic_comparison.method: Read habit, mature leaf and underside, bud, and ripe cupule together; avoid a single-leaf ID.

pair_specific_tie_breakers.quercus-sinuata-var-breviloba: Both can have variable, rounded or lobed leaves and pale bark. Lacey oak is usually taller with conspicuously blue-green/glaucous broad leaves and a barrel-like acorn; white shin often low, multi-stemmed and with a smaller nut and flatter cup scales.
pair_specific_tie_breakers.quercus-vaseyana: Vasey has narrower leathery evergreen/subevergreen leaves, usually an acute apex and often 3–5 coarse mucronate teeth per side. Vasey's much bumpier regular cup scales and dark strip-exfoliating bark are better than leaf color alone.

diagnostic_comparison.field_uncertainty: Retain Quercus sp. or the pair-level comparison if intermediates / absent fruit prevent a reliable determination.
